sentences.text:
Sudhar Singh @ Sudhar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7
November, 2025
Author: Dwarka Dhish Bansal
Bench: Dwarka Dhish Bansal

1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Jabalpur
 Cra No. 5786 of 2020
 (Sudhar Singh @ Sudhar Vs The State Of Madhya P
 Dated : 07-11-2025

Shri Devendra Kumar Gangrade - Advocate for the petitio
 Ms. Priyanka Mishra - Government Ad
 respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No.9970/2025, second application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.
His earlier application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 06.11.2023.

Appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for Life and fine of Rs.30,000/- and Section 5(n) read with Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo RI for Life with fine of Rs.20,000/-respectively, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that vide order dated 06.11.2023, this Court had granted liberty to the appellant to renew it after completion of 07 years of actual sentence as on date.
He further submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
He also submits that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He further submits that there are material contradictions and omissions 2 CRA-5786-2020 in the testimonies of the witnesses.
Appellant has no previous criminal history.
The appellant has completed more than 07 years of actual incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2020 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
Appellant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
After perusal of the record and medical reports, it seems that hymen of the prosecutrix was intact.
There is mild redness on the private part of the prosecutrix and its a case of false implication

,
therefore, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.
It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like 3 CRA-5786-2020 amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 19.02.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
(VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (AJAY KUMAR  JUDGE JUD  NP Sudhar Singh @ Sudhar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125558334/
